newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Diptheria outbreak closes Moscow school.
newsitem.headline: Diptheria outbreak closes Moscow school.

text.p: Thirty-five pupils of a Moscow school have been taken to hospital with diphtheria and the school closed for disinfection, an official said on Friday.

Once-rare illnesses such as cholera, tuberculosis and diphtheria are making a comeback in Russia and other former Soviet republics due to a fall in healthcare standards as the countries try to adapt to a market economy.
"There are 36 who are either carriers or ill with the disease, 35 are in hospital and one is at home," said Lyudmila Luchshina, head of the local epidemological inspectorate.
The school, in Moscow's Southern district, was due to reopen on Monday, said the school's director Lyudmila Kuzmina.

On Friday the classrooms were full of masked medical workers testing pupils for the disease to assess the scale of the outbreak. "Maybe we'll find more carriers over the weekend," said Luchshina. Diphtheria is an infectious throat disease which attacks the air passages.
